topics.label: Introduction and lecture framing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the complement system and frames its conceptual significance and nomenclature within the immunology course.

topics.label: Overview, nomenclature, and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational architecture of complement, covering its overarching functions, naming conventions, and the central role of C3 activation.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three biochemical recognition routes—alternative, lectin, and classical—and how they generate convertases to reach the complement activation threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream functional outcomes of complement activation, including opsonization for phagocytosis, inflammatory signalling, and pathogen lysis via the membrane attack complex.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and host protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses how regulatory proteins and inhibitory mechanisms prevent complement from damaging host cells and tissues.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how deficiencies in individual complement components and regulators produce distinct clinical phenotypes and disease risks.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the mechanisms pathogens evolve to evade complement-mediated destruction, using Staphylococcus aureus as a primary model.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up and preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session on complement and previews the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
